protocol.name: hikari_input_method_v1

description.summary: tell an input method which client is focused

protocol.description:
An input method needs to know which application it is typing into.
The standard input-method-v2 protocol deliberately does not say: its activate/deactivate events carry no arguments, so a client sees "a text input wants you" but not whose text input it is.
hikari exposes that missing piece here. An input method binds this global and receives an opaque identifier for the wl_client owning the text input that is currently focused. The identifier is assigned by the compositor and stays valid for as long as that client is connected, so an input method can keep per-application state and restore it when the user switches back.
The events here are a hint for input methods; they carry no protocol obligations and may be ignored. Compositors are free not to implement this protocol at all, which is why clients must treat the global as optional.

interface.name: hikari_input_method_v1
interface.description: One object per input method client. The compositor sends focused_client whenever a text input starts being focused, and client_gone when a client for which an identifier was allocated disconnects. A client_gone event may be sent even if this object did not receive focused_client for that identifier.

event.name: focused_client

description.summary: the client that now owns the focused text input

event.description:
Sent immediately before the corresponding zwp_input_method_v2.activate event, so a client that reads events in order always knows which application the following activate refers to. If the compositor cannot allocate an identifier, it may still send activate without a preceding focused_client; in that case the input method has no new client identity for that activation.
It is also sent right after binding, if a text input is focused at that moment, so a late-binding client does not have to wait for the next focus change to learn the current one.
id is assigned by the compositor and is never 0. It stays valid until a client_gone event with the same id arrives. The same client always gets the same id, and ids are never reused within a compositor session.

event.name: client_gone

description.summary: a client with an allocated identifier disconnected

event.description:
The client identified by id is gone; any state kept for it can be dropped. No further focused_client event will carry this id.
This event can be sent to a bound object that never received focused_client for id, for example if the identifier was allocated before that object was bound. Removing unknown state is a no-op.
Note that a client may still be the focused one when it disconnects; the compositor will follow up with a deactivate (or another focused_client) as focus moves.
